intro: Thirty-seven miracles are recorded in the four Gospels — healings, exorcisms, the dead raised, and the works over nature. John calls his seven 'signs', and ends by saying the world could not hold the books if all were written.

items.k: The first sign, at a wedding, at his mother's word.

items.n: The nobleman's son healed at a distance
items.k: 'Go thy way, thy son liveth' — the second sign.

items.n: The demoniac in the synagogue at Capernaum
items.k: The first exorcism; the spirit knows his name.
The fever leaves her, and she serves them.
'Launch out into the deep' — and Peter falls at his knees.
'I will. Be thou made clean' — and he touches him.

items.n: The paralytic lowered through the roof
items.k: 'Thy sins are forgiven thee' first; then, 'take up thy bed'.

items.n: The man at the pool of Bethesda
items.k: Thirty-eight years; healed on the Sabbath.

items.n: The man with the withered hand
items.k: Healed on the Sabbath, in the synagogue, while they watched.
'Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof' — prayed at every Mass.
The first raising of the dead: he touches the bier.
Followed by the accusation that he casts out devils by Beelzebub.
'Peace, be still.' Who is this, that wind and sea obey him?

items.n: The Gerasene demoniac and the swine
items.k: 'My name is Legion' — and two thousand pigs into the sea.

items.n: The woman with the issue of blood
items.k: She touches the hem of his garment in the crowd.
'Talitha cumi' — little girl, arise.
'According to your faith, be it done unto you.'
'Never was the like seen in Israel.'
The only miracle in all four Gospels: five loaves, two fish, twelve baskets.
'It is I, fear not' — and Peter steps out of the boat.
'Even the dogs eat the crumbs' — a Gentile mother's wit and faith.

items.n: The deaf man with the impediment
items.k: 'Ephpheta' — be opened.
Seven loaves, seven baskets, in Gentile country.
Healed in two stages: 'I see men as it were trees, walking.'
Clay and spittle, the pool of Siloam, and a trial before the Pharisees.

items.n: The boy with the demon after the Transfiguration
items.k: 'I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.'

items.n: The coin in the fish's mouth
items.k: The Temple tax paid from a fish.
Eighteen years; loosed on the Sabbath, 'this daughter of Abraham'.
At a Pharisee's table, on the Sabbath.
Ten healed, one — a Samaritan — comes back to give thanks.
'Lazarus, come forth' — four days in the tomb.
'Son of David, have mercy on me' — he throws away his cloak and runs.
The one destructive miracle, a sign against the fruitless Temple.
The last healing, in Gethsemane, of the man who came to arrest him.
A hundred and fifty-three fish, and breakfast on the shore.
The sign of Jonah: three days, and the tomb is empty.
From the Mount of Olives, a cloud, and two men in white.
